Jordan / team —

Quick notes from the Dedicated NAT gateway:
- SNAT pools look healthy by nominal counters but I do see uneven distribution across two SNAT interfaces. One pool (snat-pool-b) is handling ~70% of flows to Hearth's backend, which could explain the asymmetric return paths.
- conntrack table is at 78% of capacity; there's a spike around 09:28 (coincides with their load test).
- No explicit port exhaustion, but we do see a handful of entries with source ports rewritten unexpectedly — looks like a legacy translation rule (rule id 112) that we forgot to remove during the migration.

Actions taken:
- Disabled rule id 112 on the NAT gateway (non-breaking, high confidence) — monitoring for 10m.
- Increased conntrack limit by 25% on the gateway (temporary) and cleared stale entries for the affected 10.0.14.0/24 prefix.

Attaching route_table_snapshot.txt excerpt showing SNAT binding. Suggest we verify firewall MSS clamp next; if fragmentation is the root cause we should add an MSS clamp on the forward path (1300) and coordinate Hearth to accept PMTU blackhole mitigation.

Attachments: route_table_snapshot.txt

— Marissa Cole
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: private cutover - reachability intermittent after handoff

Team —

I pulled firewall logs and kernel dmesg from the on-prem edge (via our collector). Findings:
- Firewall had a rule-order regression where an older outbound ACL matched before the intended post-cutover rule, causing SNAT to use an overlapping /24 that Hearth also advertises. That produced asymmetric path choices for return traffic.
- ICMP fragmentation-needed packets were being rate-limited and in some cases silently dropped by the firewall appliance due to a default anti-icmp policy. That explains the PMTU blackhole behavior in the pcap.
- Security group-style ACLs on the edge were restricting ephemeral ports to 1024-49151 only; some of Hearth's newer services use ports >49152, which caused intermittent connection failures after retries.

Remediation performed:
- Reordered firewall ACLs to ensure post-cutover SNAT/egress rule takes precedence.
- Temporarily disabled ICMP rate-limiting for frag-needed on the customer-facing interface (hoping to allow PMTU discovery).
- Expanded ephemeral port range to 1024-65535 in the ACLs and added an explicit exception for Hearth's backend CIDR.

I've attached mss-trace.png (PMTU trace with and without clamp) and updated the runbook draft with a note to add a post-cutover ACL verification checklist. Recommend we keep the conntrack increase for 1 hour and monitor. If Hearth still sees instability, we do a controlled rollback to the previous egress policy (I have the pre-cutover route table snapshot).

Attachments: mss-trace.png, runbook-private-cutover.md

— Monica Patel
Security & Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
